prize_parts.citation: for empirical analyses of how import competition and technological change reshape employment, wages and adjustment in local labour markets

statement.case_for: The laureates and the ballot are unchanged: B023 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. I have narrowed the citation to what this trio can carry. The Autor-Dorn-Hanson China-shock papers are the clearest case on the shortlist of a sharp question paired with a transparent, reusable design: how import competition reaches local labour markets and workers. They contradicted the expectation of fast, frictionless reallocation. The finding of slow and costly local adjustment has been re-examined many times, including through critiques of shift-share inference, and the qualitative result has not gone away. The criterion I weigh most is that a result survives re-analysis, and I apply it equally to B006 and B047. Dorn also worked with Autor on job polarisation and local labour markets (from recall, not verified). The trio can therefore credit the technology side through jointly authored work, without claiming the skill-premium literature or the task-model theory that sits with Katz, Goldin, Acemoglu and Restrepo. On overlap with the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes, I would use one standard for B023 and B006. Overlap counts against a candidate only to the extent that the credit being claimed has already been absorbed by an earlier prize. For the China-shock core I do not see that absorption. For the Bernanke-Gertler accelerator it is partly present.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged: B023 can be read as two discoveries, the technology and wage-structure line and the trade-shock line. Narrowing the citation and keeping Dorn sharpens attribution but leaves out Katz, whose long-run wage-structure evidence is a real contribution. A narrower citation may also understate how broadly the technology-and-trade literature has shaped labour economics and policy debate. The size and persistence of the local effects and the shift-share inference are still debated, and I rely on recall for how far the core result has survived. B006, in a two- or three-name version, is a serious competitor on conceptual foundation and age. I weigh evidential transparency heavily, and my metascience background may tilt me toward designs I find easy to scrutinise. The committee could reasonably weigh breadth of conceptual influence differently without being wrong on the science.

responses.point: Hassler's own round-1 file prefers a three-name B006 (Kiyotaki, Moore, Gertler). He ties Gertler's credit to the intermediary-frictions work with Kiyotaki, wants the citation to exclude bank-run and deposit-insurance themes, and says the committee should state openly that the accelerator credit is partly absorbed. He ranks B023 below B006 because its credit spans tasks and trade shocks and the Katz, Dorn and Acemoglu boundaries.
responses.response: In my round-1 reply I treated him as proposing a two-name award. That was wrong, and I now anchor on his file, as the chair summary asks. The citation discipline he describes, collateral and balance-sheet frictions with the accelerator and bank-run themes explicitly set aside, is the right way to handle the 2022 overlap. It makes B006 more competitive than my round-1 reply suggested. Whether Gertler's post-accelerator work is separable is a question for the macro specialists, and I cannot judge it. It does not reverse my ordering, because I weight designs that can be re-analysed, and he himself calls identification of the collateral channel mixed. His boundary critique of B023 is fair, and I have answered it by narrowing the citation to evidence on local labour-market adjustment, keeping Dorn, and not claiming the task-model theory.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B006 first. He argues that a mechanism need not be settled in every empirical detail to be prize-worthy if it organised a large research programme and survived the 2008 test. On B023 he says he would favour a version that stays within one of the two strands, to keep the citation precise, and he names Dorn as the most obvious omission.
responses.response: I accept his point that a conceptual contribution can be prize-worthy without settled empirical identification. Our difference is in weighting, not in a decisive scientific gap. I take his suggestion to stay within one strand seriously, and my narrowed citation is partly a response to it. I anchor it in the trade-shock core and in jointly authored work on local labour markets, and I do not claim the skill-premium or task-model literature. I would add that the 2008 crisis is one very large test, but it does not isolate the specific collateral channel. That is why I weigh the repeatedly re-analysed China-shock designs somewhat more heavily. I hold that as a judgement, not a demonstration.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B023 first with Autor, Hanson and Katz. He says Katz anchors the technology side that a Dorn trio would not credit. He would not object to Dorn instead of Katz under a narrower citation, and he regards the third name as an open attribution choice.
responses.response: We agree on the Autor-Hanson core, and the third name is the live question. I keep Dorn. He co-authored the central China-shock papers and, from my recall, the Autor-Dorn polarisation work, so the technology side is not left wholly uncredited. Katz's wage-structure evidence is a genuine contribution, but it overlaps with a tradition that has already been recognised. Whether that outweighs Dorn's claim is a judgement, and I do not think it is settled. I am glad his reading leaves room for the swap. I would not want the committee to treat a Katz-Dorn choice as a technicality.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B023 eighth only because of its attribution structure. He says that if the committee wants a labour award he would favour a citation limited to the trade-shock strand, where credit is clearer, over a bundle that omits Dorn or Katz.
responses.response: This is partial convergence. His objection is about attribution, not about the quality of the science, and my narrower citation moves toward his preference. I stop short of dropping the technology strand entirely. As I recall, Autor and Dorn's polarisation work shares the local-labour-market design and authors with the China-shock papers. I would accept a pure trade-shock wording if the committee finds that cleaner, since the Autor-Dorn-Hanson core is unchanged by the choice. I agree with him that breadth of public influence should not substitute for a sharply attributable result.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson ranks B047 first. She replies to Krusell that BLP's identifying assumptions are explicit and are probed through sensitivity analysis and validation against merger retrospectives. Her own B023 proposal names Autor, Hanson and Dorn.
responses.response: Validation against merger retrospectives is the kind of evidence I weight, and it softens my round-1 worry about functional-form dependence in structural IO. I cannot verify from the supplied evidence how systematically counterfactuals have been validated. From a metascience view I would still want to know how sensitive estimates are across independent analysts. That is why B047 is not on my list, but I do not treat it as scientifically weaker than B023. Our shared preference for Dorn as the third name on the labour ballot is a point of agreement, and I do not use it as support for B023.

uncertainties: Whether the committee reads B023 as one achievement about how shocks to labour demand reach workers and places, or as two strands that should not share a citation, and whether the narrowed wording resolves this.
Whether Dorn or Katz should be the third name. I rely on recall of authorship patterns and have not verified contribution or citation data.

How large and persistent the local China-shock effects are and how robust the shift-share inference is. I believe the qualitative result has survived, but I cannot verify this from the supplied evidence.

Whether Gertler's post-accelerator work is separable from the Bernanke-Gertler line, which decides whether B006 is better as a two- or three-name prize. I cannot judge this and defer to the macro members.
How to weigh transparent, re-analysable evidence against conceptual foundation across B023, B006 and B047. My weighting is a judgement that colleagues could reasonably make differently.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. None apparent from my supplied profile. My listed co-authors and affiliations (Johannesson, Ellingsen, Brodeur and the Institute for Replication, Camerer, Rand, Nowak, Fudenberg, Pfeiffer, Holzmeister, Huber, Nosek and Johan Almenberg) are not credited names on any shortlisted ballot. I share an SSE affiliation with committee colleagues Andersson, Friberg and Strömberg, and Johannesson, a former committee member, is my main co-author. I disclose these as collegial ties without adjudicating them. My metascience orientation may lead me to weight evidential transparency more than colleagues do. I disclose that as a perspective and not as evidence of merit.
